title: Colorado Wildfires- Army Fire Breaks
description:
The Department of Defense provides firefighting support for the Colorado Springs area.  U.S. Army members from the 52nd Engineering Battalion at Fort Carson use bulldozers to create a fire break near a hiking trail on the west border of the Air Force Academy grounds. 
Interview with 1LT Cameron Rohrer, U.S. Army.
keywords: Colorado wildfires, Coloradofire, Waldo Canyon Fire, 52nd Engineering Battalion, 1LT Cameron Rohrer, Air Force Academy, firefighting, bulldozer

transcript.text: So out here today we got about five dozers around the Academy at three different spots right now.
We're establishing containment lines along the western border of the Air Force Academy.
The purpose is to prevent the fire from, if it moves down towards the Academy,
from the hills to the west, to contain it from jumping onto the Academy's grounds.
At that point it would be tough to control where the damage happens with a lot of,
you know, structures and homes.
So yesterday we cleared about four kilometers further southeast.
About eight, those are blades wide.
And today we're working four kilometers here, about three or four further north,
and then two or three down further south.
The idea is one line that's completely solid along the entire border of the Academy
and keeping the fire out.
We came out Tuesday and all the equipment came up Wednesday morning,
and all of our guys have been out there out here since working from early morning to late at night.
So we've been hard at work and it feels good to help another sister service,
so we're all on this together.
Safety is obviously the most important thing.
We make sure everyone's properly equipped, both on the equipment and those guiding them around.
And of course keeping them hydrated in the heat and fed and rested.
It's tough, but we're pulling it off and accomplishing the mission.
It's an ongoing operation, especially as some equipment goes down
and we take it back to the unit and try and get it up as quick as we can.
There have been basically three pushes of equipment up here.
The first had three dozers and then five more came yesterday, looking for two more today.
So they've all got work to do.
It's hugely important because it's basically the last line of defense in an important area, such as around here.
And what it means to me, it's been a phenomenal opportunity.
The soldiers are doing great work and working really hard.
And it's been impressive to see how much they're all working together
and also at the higher levels between different services.
I think there's been a lot of good talks so that we're all trying to achieve the same goal.

pass_reason: Bulldozers cutting a fire break plus interview; no visible danger or outcome.
